newsitem.title: BRAZIL: BRAZIL DEBT OUTLOOK - Swap talk hits the road.
newsitem.headline: BRAZIL DEBT OUTLOOK - Swap talk hits the road.

text.p: Brazilian officials were expected Tuesday to kick off a three-day roadshow in New York for the nation's upcoming 30-year global bond, which may be bought outright or swapped for existing Brady bonds.
Central Bank International Affairs Director Gustavo Franco will explain the deal this week to investors in New York, Boston and London, a bank spokesman said.
The swap offer, announced last week, has perked up Brazilian Bradies, which have consistently underperformed Argentina and Mexico the past several months.

Brazilian Bradies were expected to remain well supported until the June 3 swap deadline, although there seemed to be more interest in Pars BR4D24=RR and Discs BRFLTD24=RR than Cs BR8D14=RR. Investors can exchange the three bonds for the new global issue.
Cs were seen the least attractive swap option because unlike Pars and Discs, they are uncollateralized and an exchange would not be as lucrative to investors.
The new issue is expected to range between $1 billion and $4 billion, although no upper limit has been set.

Following the announcement of the Brady buyback, no one was certain when Brazil's 500 billion Italian lira 20-year bond would be launched. Deutsche Morgan Grenfell is lead managing the bond, which was originally scheduled for May and then pushed back to early June.

-- Industrial group Votorantim -- a $300 million eight-year bond, five-year put, sometime in June, sources close to the deal said. The bond will be guaranteed by five companies in the group, including Votorantim Celulose e Papel.
ING Barings is leading the deal and the roadshow was scheduled to get under way this week in Europe and next week in the United States.

-- Sao Paulo state power company Cesp -- a $200 million eight-year bond, putable and callable at five, seen pricing sometime in June, a Cesp official said Monday. The bond, which has been put off since March, is the first of a $500 million program Cesp plans this year. J.P. Morgan is leading the first issue.
IN SECONDARY TRADE, Brazilian Eurobonds performed well on news of the Brady buyback. Brazil's 8.875 percent global due 2001 ZQ4P tightened 17 bps to a record 151 bps over U.S. Treasuries.
Brazil outperformed Mexico's 9.75 percent 2001 ZM5W, which tightened three bps to 142 over, and Argentina's 9.25 percent 2001 ZN4D, which narrowed six bps to 142 over.

Brazilian corporates also performed well. ING Barings said in its weekly report from Sao Paulo that the media and electricity sectors narrowed 20 bps on average; steel tightened 15 bps across the board; food narrowed 12 bps, and paper and pulp tightened 10 bps on average.

STILL CHEAP AFTER the run-up, according to traders, was Furnas' 9.0 percent due 2005 (put 02) ZXLW, which was trading at 230 bps over. Furnas is guaranteed by Eletrobras and should trade about 20 to 25 bps over Eletrobras' 10 percent due 2004 (put 01) ZSED, now trading at 195 bps over Treasuries.
